gaps.sentence: He works as a waiter ___ studying for his degree.
gaps.explanation: 'While' joins two ongoing actions; 'during' takes a noun.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we arrived ___ the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly... when' is the fixed pair for one event interrupting another.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: ___ she now lives in Oslo, she still supports the Dublin club.
gaps.explanation: 'Although' introduces the contrasting clause; 'despite' needs a noun phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ his age, he still plays football every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite his age' — noun phrase after despite.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
The hotel is comfortable; ___, it is far too expensive.
I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.
